payload.title: David's charge to Solomon

aliases: the anointed of the God of Jacob
payload.name: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)
payload.note: The single David of the Hebrew books and the New Testament references: son of Jesse, shepherd, harpist, anointed king, father of Solomon; all entries describe this one king and the hint's second David is not needed.

stages.label: David as king

quotes.quote: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

stages.text: David: a man of about thirty to fifty, athletic and broad-shouldered, of medium height; ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes, short dark beard trimmed close; dark hair cut to the shoulder. Signature outfit: a long blue royal robe with a sash of crimson and gold, over an undertunic of white linen. Carries a bronze-bossed sword in a leather scabbard and a harp.

stages.label: David as youth

quotes.quote: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Yahweh said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”

stages.text: David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.

stages.label: David as elder

quotes.quote: Now King David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.

stages.text: David: an old man of about seventy, lean and bent with age, his frame still dignified; ruddy complexion faded to a weathered warmth, dark eyes deep-set and gentle, white hair and a white beard cut short. Signature outfit: a plain long wool robe of undyed cream with a dark blue cloak over the shoulders for warmth. Carries a staff of almond wood.

payload.name: Solomon
payload.note: Son of David and Bathsheba, king of Israel who builds the temple; the same individual across all divisions. Distinguish from the Shulammite's shepherd beloved, who is not Solomon.

stages.label: Solomon, king of Israel

quotes.quote: had Solomon ride on King David’s mule, and brought him to Gihon.
sat down on his throne and caused a throne to be set for the king’s mother

stages.text: Solomon: man in his twenties to forties, lean and upright with a composed, dignified bearing; warm olive-brown skin; dark curly hair and a short, neatly trimmed beard; calm, thoughtful face with a broad brow. Signature outfit: a long deep-blue royal court robe with gold-thread borders over a white linen tunic, and a gold circlet on his head. Signature prop: a plain rod of royal authority carried alone.

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
payload.name: Jerusalem
payload.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

payload.title: Fountain opened and the struck shepherd
Keep the king's command

payload.name: Under the sun
payload.note: The general setting of earthly human activity described throughout; not a single place.

stages.label: Under the sun

quotes.quote: under the sun
all that is done under the sky
If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth

stages.text: Under the sun: a wide, sun-bleached Levantine earth of dry hill country and terraced fields, with stone walls, olive and terebinth trees, winding river beds, and distant walled cities of pale limestone beneath an open sky.

payload.title: Fire from heaven and God's promise

aliases: the house which is called by my name
the tent of the daughter of Zion
the house of Yahweh of Armies
payload.name: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple)
payload.note: The one Jerusalem temple (Yahweh's house, the sanctuary on Mount Moriah) across all references, from Solomon's building through repair, destruction and rebuilding; construction and ruin are later appearance stages, not separate places.

stages.label: Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah

quotes.quote: The house, when it was under construction, was built of stone prepared at the quarry
Within the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in its height.
He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.
Also he made before the house two pillars thirty-five cubits high
He set the sea on the right side of the house eastward and toward the south.

stages.text: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

payload.title: Promise of restoration

payload.name: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah
payload.note: Prophet from Anathoth who speaks most of the book.

stages.label: Jeremiah

quotes.quote: The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
They let down Jeremiah with cords. In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire.

stages.text: Jeremiah: a man in his middle years, lean and weathered from long journeys and imprisonment, with a grave, careworn face and deep-set dark eyes. Close-cropped dark hair and a short greying beard. Dark-skinned Levantine complexion. Wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic under a long brown wool cloak, the cloak worn thin at the hem. Carries a plain wooden staff.

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
payload.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
payload.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

payload.title: Commissioning of Joshua, the Song, and the sentence on Moses

payload.name: Moses
payload.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

payload.name: Joshua son of Nun
payload.note: Son of Nun of Ephraim, Moses' aide and successor who leads Israel into Canaan; the same individual across Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges (as the deceased) and Hebrews, so no other Joshua is separated from him in this group.

stages.label: Joshua son of Nun

quotes.quote: Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, didn’t depart from the Tent.
Joshua was old and well advanced in years

stages.text: Joshua son of Nun: a man of mature strength in his prime, aged about forty to fifty when leading, with a sturdy, broad-shouldered build and weathered brown skin marked by desert sun. Short dark hair, close-cropped beard, steady deep-set eyes and a firm, grave face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic and a dark brown woven wool cloak. Carries a bronze-bladed sword at his belt and a long wooden spear.

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
payload.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
payload.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

aliases: the priests who bear the ark
payload.name: The priests and Levites (Deuteronomy)
payload.note: The Levitical priests who bear the ark and minister and judge in Deuteronomy's ritual and legal scenes.

stages.label: The priests and Levites

quotes.quote: the priests the sons of Levi, who bore the ark of Yahweh’s covenant
You shall command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant

stages.text: The priests and Levites: adult men of middle age, sturdy and dignified; olive-brown skin of the Levant; close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard; calm, grave features. Signature outfit: a white woven linen tunic and sash with a blue-violet priestly robe and cloak, plain and clean. Carry the ark's poles on the shoulder.

payload.name: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy
payload.note: Tribal judges and officers who hear cases and receive the law in Deuteronomy.

stages.label: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy

quotes.quote: then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before Yahweh, before the priests and the judges
then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place.

stages.text: Elders, judges and officers: men of middle to advanced age, mostly weathered and grey-bearded; sturdy build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beards and close-cropped hair; calm, serious faces. Signature outfit: a long woven undertunic of undyed linen under a deep indigo cloak with a plain woven border. Carry a short wooden staff of office.

payload.name: The plains of Moab
payload.note: Eastern camp across the Jordan where Moses speaks the law and dies, Deuteronomy only.

stages.label: The plains of Moab

quotes.quote: Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to declare this law
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is opposite Jericho.
in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites

stages.text: The plains of Moab: a broad, low valley of dry grassland and scrub east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho and Beth Peor, with acacia, tamarisk and wild shrubs along the river line. Rising to the west, the bare slopes of Mount Nebo and Pisgah, with a flat-topped summit, look over the Jordan valley. Plain tents of goat hair and rough stone walls mark the Israelite encampment; no buildings of note stand in the valley.

payload.name: Mount Nebo and Pisgah
payload.note: Mountain heights east of the Jordan in Numbers where Balaam views Israel and Moses views the land; distinct from the Israelite mountains and Edom.

stages.label: Mount Nebo and Pisgah

quotes.quote: He took him into the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars
under the slopes of Pisgah eastward.
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is opposite Jericho.

stages.text: Mount Nebo and Pisgah: a bare, rounded ridge of pale limestone rising east of the Jordan in the highlands of Moab, its upper slopes broken by grey outcrops and scattered scrub. Below its flanks the Arabah stretches toward the Salt Sea. On the summit stand low, rough-hewn stone altars and a few dry terraces, with no town or dwelling in view.

payload.title: Jotham's reign

payload.name: Jotham
payload.note: King of Judah son of Uzziah who builds the upper gate.

stages.label: Jotham, king of Judah

quotes.quote: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.

stages.text: Jotham: man in his mid-twenties to forties; sturdy, upright build; olive-brown skin; short dark beard trimmed close, dark hair bound back at the nape; calm, steady face with a broad brow. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of undyed linen under a deep indigo royal cloak with a woven band at the hem; a gold circlet at the brow. Carries a plain bronze-bound staff of office.

payload.title: Jerusalem as an unfaithful foundling wife

payload.name: Ezekiel son of Buzi
payload.note: Exiled priest and prophet at the river Chebar.

stages.label: Ezekiel son of Buzi

quotes.quote: Yahweh’s word came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar

stages.text: Ezekiel son of Buzi: a man of about thirty, lean and steady, with dark hair and a short trimmed beard, bronze-brown skin from desert sun, and a calm, watchful face. He wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic with a long cloak of rough brown wool over it. He carries a wooden writing tablet and stylus.

payload.title: Paul's sermon at Antioch of Pisidia

payload.name: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)
payload.note: Pharisee from Tarsus who persecutes the Way, is converted on the road to Damascus, and becomes the apostle Paul; told apart from the king by his Pharisee and Tarsus background and conversion narrative in Acts.

stages.label: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)

quotes.quote: The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.
I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees.
But I was born a Roman.

stages.text: Saul/Paul: man in his thirties to fifties, middle height and spare, wiry build worn by travel and hardship. Olive-brown skin, dark hair cropped short, close-trimmed dark beard with grey beginning at the chin. Lined forehead, deep-set dark eyes, strong nose. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark brown travelling cloak with a fringed hem. Signature prop: a worn leather writing satchel and a plain wooden walking staff.

payload.name: Barnabas
payload.note: Levite of Cyprus, also called Joses, who travels with Paul.

stages.label: Barnabas

quotes.quote: a Levite, a man of Cyprus by race

stages.text: Barnabas: a man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and steady, with a weathered olive-brown skin from sea and road. Short dark hair going grey at the temples, and a neatly trimmed dark beard. Calm, warm eyes and a broad, open face. He wears a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long cream-brown wool cloak. Carries a worn leather travelling satchel and a wooden staff.

payload.name: Crowd in Acts
payload.note: The crowd gathering in Jerusalem, Ephesus, Lystra and elsewhere to hear, mock or riot in Acts.

stages.label: Crowd in Acts

quotes.quote: the multitude came together and were bewildered, because everyone heard them speaking in his own language.
for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”

stages.text: Crowd in Acts: a typical member is an adult of about twenty to fifty years, lean and sun-browned from working outdoors, with dark brown or black hair worn short or tied back and beards kept short on men. Skin olive to tawny, faces weathered and serious. Clothing: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre or earth-brown, a dark wool cloak in deep blue or grey, sandals. Carries no props of his own.

payload.name: Antioch of Pisidia
payload.note: City in Pisidia (Asia Minor) where Paul preaches in the synagogue and turns to the Gentiles; distinct from Antioch of Syria by region.

stages.label: Antioch of Pisidia

quotes.quote: they, passing on from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia
They went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day and sat down.

stages.text: Antioch of Pisidia: a Roman colonial city on a high plateau of Pisidia in Asia Minor, ringed by rugged limestone mountains capped with snow. Pale stone city walls and wide paved streets lined with colonnades of white marble, Roman civic buildings with tiled roofs, and a stone synagogue of plain dressed masonry near the centre. Olive groves, cypress and oleander grow on the slopes; dry grass and scrub cover the plateau beyond.

payload.title: The covenant at Horeb and the ten commandments

aliases: the mountain that might be touched
payload.name: Horeb/Mount Sinai
payload.note: The single mountain of God where the law and covenant are given; all listed entries (Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, Malachi, Hebrews) refer to the same mountain under the names Horeb, Sinai, God's mountain, referenced across divisions.

stages.label: Horeb/Mount Sinai

quotes.quote: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire
You shall set bounds to the people all around
the cloud covered it six days
The mountain burned with fire to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

stages.text: Horeb/Mount Sinai: a single steep granite mountain rising from a stark desert wilderness of rock and sand; its lower slopes are broken boulders and gravel, its upper peak sharp and dark, with a cloud-wrapped summit. The base is marked by a rocky plain where the people camp, bounded by stones. No vegetation beyond scattered desert shrub; the mountain has no buildings.

payload.title: Saul's army and the Philistine threat

payload.name: Saul
payload.note: First king of Israel, son of Kish.

stages.label: Saul, first king of Israel

quotes.quote: Am I not a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel?
Saul disguised himself and put on other clothing
they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

stages.text: Saul: a man in his forties, tall and broad-shouldered with a strong, weathered face, dark hair cut to the neck and a short, close beard. Skin olive-brown from sun. Dignified, brooding eyes. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of deep blue wool under a dark red royal cloak with a gold-bordered hem, a bronze-scaled leather belt and a plain sandal. Carries a royal spear of dark ash wood with a bronze head.

payload.name: Jonathan son of Saul
payload.note: Eldest son of King Saul and close friend of David; the same man across Samuel and Chronicles, killed with Saul on Gilboa. Distinguish from other Jonathans by being Saul's son and David's covenant friend.

stages.label: Jonathan son of Saul

quotes.quote: Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was on him and gave it to David with his clothing, even including his sword, his bow, and his sash.
Jonathan the son of Saul said to the young man who bore his armor

stages.text: Jonathan son of Saul: a young man in his twenties, tall and lean, strong-shouldered from war; olive skin, dark close-cropped hair and a short trimmed beard; open, steady face with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a linen tunic in deep blue over which he wears a sleeveless bronze-scaled warrior's coat, with a crimson sash. Carries alone a curved bow of dark wood and a sword in a leather sheath.

payload.name: Samuel
payload.note: Son of Hannah raised at Shiloh, judge and prophet who anoints Saul and David; the child of Eli's temple, not Elkanah.

stages.label: Samuel as a boy at Shiloh

quotes.quote: The child was young.
The child served Yahweh before Eli the priest.
The child Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with Yahweh and also with men.

stages.text: Samuel: a boy of about ten years, slight and sturdy, with warm brown skin, short dark curly hair and clear, attentive eyes. His signature outfit is a plain undyed linen tunic of pale ochre with a short linen ephod-style sash, bare feet. He carries no props.

stages.label: Samuel as judge and prophet

quotes.quote: Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpah.
Fill your horn with oil, and go.
Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

stages.text: Samuel: a man in his middle years, lean and upright, with weathered brown skin, a close-trimmed dark beard flecked with grey, short hair and calm, steady eyes. His signature outfit is a long undyed linen tunic belted at the waist under a deep blue wool cloak. He carries a horn of oil at his belt and, on journeys, a plain wooden staff.

payload.name: Philistines
payload.note: The oppressors of Israel and lords of the Philistines in Samson's story; a foreign people, not an Israelite tribe.

stages.label: Philistines (typical warrior of the lords' armies)

quotes.quote: the five lords of the Philistines
thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen

stages.text: Philistines: adult men of the coastal cities, age twenty to forty; medium-to-broad build, sun-browned skin; close-cropped dark hair and a short beard; calm, hard-set features, not caricatured. Typical dress: a knee-length woven tunic of undyed wool with a bordered hem in blue or red, a leather belt and a short cloak of dark wool. Signature props: a bronze helmet with a crest and a round shield, carried by the army; no props carried by the figure alone.

payload.name: Gilgal (Saul's coronation and rejection)
payload.note: Site in 1 Samuel where Saul is made king, offers sacrifice and is rebuked by Samuel.

stages.label: Gilgal

quotes.quote: He went from year to year in a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah
All the people went to Gilgal; and there they made Saul king before Yahweh in Gilgal.

stages.text: Gilgal: a low, open limestone plateau in the Jordan valley near Jericho, with scattered grey standing stones and a rough stone altar of unhewn rock. Terebinth and tamarisk trees at its edges, dry grass, a few mud-brick and fieldstone houses on the rise. Bethel and Mizpah lie on the hills to the west.

payload.name: Gibeah of Saul (1 Samuel)
payload.note: Saul's home town and royal seat in 1 Samuel, where Saul is found, anointed and later fights the Philistines at Michmash; distinguish from the Judges Gibeah by its link to Saul and the monarchy.

stages.label: Gibeah of Saul

quotes.quote: Saul also went to his house in Gibeah
under the pomegranate tree which is in Migron
Saul was sitting in Gibeah, under the tamarisk tree in Ramah

stages.text: Gibeah of Saul: a fortified hill town of Benjamin on a rocky ridge in the central highlands. Stone-walled terraces climb the slopes, flat-roofed houses of limestone and mudbrick cluster near a citadel tower at the crest, and a town gate faces the approach road. Terebinth and pomegranate trees grow at the edge of the upper town, with a tamarisk tree in the open ground below, and hills of scrub and olive fall away eastward toward the wilderness.

payload.name: Michmash
payload.note: Philistine garrison place where Jonathan attacks.

stages.label: Michmash

quotes.quote: The one crag rose up on the north in front of Michmash, and the other on the south in front of Geba.
They came up and encamped in Michmash, eastward of Beth Aven.
The garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.

stages.text: Michmash: a narrow limestone pass cut between steep chalk crags, one rising on the north and one on the south, with a dry wadi floor below. Scattered terraced hillside, low thorn scrub, olive and terebinth clinging to the rock. Rough stone walls and a few squat mud-brick and fieldstone dwellings on the ridge. Sun-bleached pale ochre and grey stone, dusty olive green.

payload.name: Geba
payload.note: Town where Jonathan strikes the Philistine garrison.

stages.label: Geba of Benjamin

quotes.quote: Jonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba
Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people who were present with them, stayed in Geba of Benjamin
The one crag rose up on the north in front of Michmash, and the other on the south in front of Geba.

stages.text: Geba: a fortified hill-town on a rocky spur of the central Judean-Benjamite highlands, terraced limestone slopes with olive and terebinth trees. Stone-built houses of rough-hewn limestone with flat roofs cluster around a gate tower and a watchpost on the crest. Across a steep wadi to the north-east stands the crag of Michmash; a bare cliff face and a rocky ridge fall away to the south.

payload.title: Promise of Isaac and Ishmael's blessing

aliases: Abraham the father of many nations
payload.name: Abram
payload.note: Son of Terah from Ur, called to Canaan and renamed Abraham; the same patriarch as Galatians' Abraham, so both entries form one cluster.

stages.label: Abram / Abraham

quotes.quote: Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
Abraham was one hundred years old when his son, Isaac, was born to him.
Abraham gave up his spirit, and died at a good old age, an old man, and full of years
Lot went with him.

stages.text: Abram, later Abraham: an elderly man of seventy-five to one hundred years and beyond; lean, weathered build from years of travel; dark skin tanned by desert sun; short greying beard and hair; deep-set, steady eyes and lined face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed wool wrap over a earth-brown linen tunic, leather sandals. Signature prop: a long wooden herder's staff.

payload.name: Sarai/Sarah, wife of Abraham
payload.note: Wife of Abram, barren until she bears Isaac in old age and renamed Sarah; the same woman is cited in Romans, Hebrews and 1 Peter as Abraham's wife.

stages.label: Sarai / Sarah

quotes.quote: I know that you are a beautiful woman to look at.
Sarai was barren. She had no child.
her name shall be Sarah.
Abraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in age.

stages.text: Sarah: a woman of about sixty to ninety, slender and upright, with dark skin of the Ancient Near East. Her face is fine-boned and dignified, with a calm, serious gaze. Her hair is dark, bound under a plain linen headcloth, with a few grey strands showing at the temples. Her signature outfit is a long undyed wool tunic in ochre with a dark brown woollen shawl over the shoulders. She carries no props.

aliases: the hill country of the Amorites
payload.name: Canaan
payload.note: The promised land of Israel as a whole, the land Yahweh gives to Abram's descendants, referred to in Genesis, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Judges and Hebrews alike; all six entries describe this same land.

stages.label: Canaan, the promised land

quotes.quote: Surely it flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
Behold, Yahweh your God has set the land before you.
to the Western Sea
the land where you are traveling, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession
seven nations greater and mightier than you

stages.text: Canaan: a fertile hill country between the Jordan river and the Western Sea, with terraced slopes, olive groves, vineyards heavy with grapes, wheat fields in the valleys, and wells beside walled mud-brick and stone towns on the hilltops. Scattered oaks and terebinths mark old sacred places, and herders' pastures roll toward the distant coast.

payload.title: Monthly divisions, tribal captains and royal officers

payload.name: Joab
payload.note: Son of Zeruiah and David's army commander, who kills Abner, Absalom and Amasa and leads the Ammonite campaign; distinguish from other Joabs by his role as David's commander in the army.

stages.label: Joab, captain of David's army

quotes.quote: Joab was clothed in his apparel of war that he had put on, and on it was a sash with a sword fastened on his waist in its sheath
He took three darts in his hand and thrust them through Absalom’s heart
Ten young men who bore Joab’s armor surrounded and struck Absalom

stages.text: Joab: a man in his middle years, around forty to fifty, of strong, weathered build with broad shoulders and a soldier's stance. Skin olive-brown and sun-browned. Dark hair cropped short at the neck, with a close-trimmed beard streaked with grey at the chin. Hard, watchful face with a broken nose. Signature outfit: a bronze-scaled or leather-plated military coat over a dark undertunic, with a deep red-brown war sash at the waist. Carries a sword in a plain sheath and three darts in hand.

payload.name: Benaiah son of Jehoiada (Kings)
payload.note: Captain of David's army and guard who carries out Solomon's executions in 1 Kings; the same Benaiah son of Jehoiada named here as one of the mighty men and later bodyguard commander.

stages.label: Benaiah son of Jehoiada

quotes.quote: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done mighty deeds
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did these things and had a name among the three mighty men.

stages.text: Benaiah son of Jehoiada: a seasoned man of about forty to fifty, broad-shouldered and sturdy from years of combat, with dark skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard shot with grey, a weathered, steady face with a firm mouth and deep-set eyes. His signature outfit is a plain undyed linen tunic under a dark brown wool cloak with a deep red border, with bronze scale armour and a leather belt; he wears a bronze helmet. He carries a bronze-headed spear and a curved sword.

payload.name: Ahithophel
payload.note: David's counselor from 2 Samuel who defects to Absalom's revolt, gives the counsel that is rejected in favor of Hushai's, and hangs himself; identified by the Gilonite alias and the Absalom conspiracy sections.

stages.label: Ahithophel the Gilonite

quotes.quote: Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, from his city, even from Giloh
The counsel of Ahithophel, which he gave in those days, was as if a man inquired at the inner sanctuary of God.

stages.text: Ahithophel the Gilonite: man in his fifties to sixties; lean, spare build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked dark hair and a close-trimmed grey beard; lined forehead and a grave, austere face. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a dark blue wool court cloak with a narrow ochre border. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: Hushai the Archite
payload.note: David's friend and adviser who was sent back to Absalom to defeat Ahithophel's counsel; the same Hushai appears in both entries, so they are one individual.

stages.label: Hushai the Archite

quotes.quote: Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his tunic torn and earth on his head.
Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend.

stages.text: Hushai the Archite: man in his middle years, lean and steady; olive-brown skin weathered by travel; short dark-grey-streaked beard, close-cut hair; grave, watchful face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: undyed linen tunic with a plain brown woollen cloak in earth tones; a torn tunic and dust on the head in grief. Carries no props beyond a plain walking staff.

payload.title: Greatness and a child

aliases: the apostle and high priest of our confession
the great shepherd of the sheep
the author and perfecter of faith
the mediator of a new covenant
the Lion of the tribe of Judah
the rider called Faithful and True
KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS
payload.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord
payload.note: The one Jesus: the teacher from Nazareth of the Gospels and Acts, and the risen, exalted Christ and Lord of the epistles and Revelation; the same individual across all divisions, with death, resurrection and changed portrayal not creating new individuals.

stages.label: Adult Jesus

quotes.quote: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,

stages.text: Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.

stages.label: Infant Jesus

quotes.quote: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

stages.text: Jesus: newborn to about two years old; olive-brown skin, a little dark hair and dark eyes; a small infant or toddler's build, no beard. Plain undyed swaddling linen for the newborn; a small plain linen tunic as a toddler. No adult clothing or props.

stages.label: Boy Jesus

quotes.quote: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;

stages.text: Jesus: boy of about twelve, slim and sturdy; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut short at the neck; dark eyes; no beard; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak; no props.

payload.name: The Twelve Disciples (collective)
payload.note: The twelve apostles/disciples as one collective body acting together across the Gospels and Acts; distinct from the individual disciples named within them.

stages.label: The Twelve Disciples (collective)

quotes.quote: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these. The first, Simon, who is called Peter; Andrew, his brother; James the son of Zebedee
One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him,

stages.text: The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic and a rough brown wool cloak with fringed hem. Signature props: a fishing net coiled over one shoulder for Peter and Andrew; a walking staff for travelers.

payload.name: Capernaum
payload.note: The lakeside town in Galilee where Jesus lives, teaches and heals, with a synagogue and Simon Peter's house; all four Gospels' entries describe this one place.

stages.label: Capernaum

quotes.quote: Leaving Nazareth, he came and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali
They went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath day he entered into the synagogue and taught.
They entered into the boat, and were going over the sea to Capernaum.

stages.text: Capernaum: a fishing town of plain basalt and limestone houses with flat roofs, packed close along a curving shore of the Sea of Galilee. A white limestone synagogue with a tall carved doorway stands near the water, its pillars facing the lake. Nearby, a modest family house of stone with a courtyard and reed-thatched roof marks Simon's home. Fishing boats are drawn up on the stones, nets hung on poles. Olive trees, palms and fig trees grow on the slopes behind the town, with dry hills rising beyond.

payload.title: Foxes, the men of Judah, and the jawbone

payload.name: Samson
payload.note: Nazirite judge of Dan whose exploits against the Philistines include the riddle, the foxes, the jawbone, and the temple of Dagon.

stages.label: Samson

quotes.quote: No razor shall come on his head, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb.
The woman bore a son and named him Samson. The child grew, and Yahweh blessed him.
No razor has ever come on my head; for I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb.

stages.text: Samson: a strong man in his prime, roughly thirty years old, broad-shouldered and powerfully muscled with a lean, weathered frame; sun-browned olive skin; long, uncut hair falling past his shoulders, dark brown, and a full untrimmed beard; a grave, dignified face with a strong nose and deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a woven undyed linen tunic in ochre with a plain brown wool cloak. Signature prop: none he carries; his only sign is the unshorn hair.

payload.name: Judah (tribe)
payload.note: The tribe of Judah in Judges, leading the attacks on Canaanite cities; the same tribal group as the southern kingdom addressed in Hosea, so one cluster is applied to both entries.

stages.label: Judah (tribe)

quotes.quote: Judah shall go up. Behold, I have delivered the land into his hand.
Yahweh was with Judah, and drove out the inhabitants of the hill country

stages.text: Judah: a tribe of Israel's highland men, typically adult, seasoned and sun-browned, of lean and sturdy build, with olive to tan skin, short dark hair and close-cut beards. Faces are weathered and resolute. Signature dress: undyed or earth-brown woven wool tunic belted with cord, over it a dark brown cloak of woven goat hair, with a leather sling or short sword at the belt. Shared props: round shields of wood and hide, slung leather bags for stones.

payload.name: Timnah (Philistine town)
payload.note: Philistine town where Samson takes a wife, kills a lion and sets his riddle; distinct from the Judahite Timnah of Genesis.

stages.label: Timnah, Philistine town

quotes.quote: Samson went down to Timnah, and saw a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines.
came to the vineyards of Timnah; and behold, a young lion roared at him.

stages.text: Timnah: a walled Philistine town on a low ridge of the Shephelah, with mud-brick and stone houses, flat roofs and a gate of heavy timber. Terraced vineyards of trained vines and olive trees climb the slopes beyond the town, with rough stone walls between them and scrub and rocky hollows in the lower ground.

payload.name: cave in Etam's rock
payload.note: Cave where Samson hides from the men of Judah.

stages.label: Cave in Etam's rock

quotes.quote: he went down and lived in the cave in Etam’s rock.
went down to the cave in Etam’s rock

stages.text: Cave in Etam's rock: a rugged limestone outcrop in the hill country of Judah, its grey stone weathered and broken into ledges. The cave mouth is a low, irregular opening in the cliff face, shaded by scrub oak, terebinth and wild thorn growing from cracks in the rock. Loose stones and dry grass lie at the foot of the escarpment, with the wider hills rising in terraces beyond.

payload.name: Lehi
payload.note: Place where Samson kills a thousand men with a jawbone and drinks from a spring.

stages.label: Lehi

quotes.quote: the Philistines went up, encamped in Judah, and spread themselves in Lehi.
God split the hollow place that is in Lehi, and water came out of it.

stages.text: Lehi: a rough, sunlit hill country of Judah, with low ridges of pale limestone, scattered scrub, terebinth and wild grass in the dry hollows. A broad flat clearing of packed earth lies among the rocks, where a cleft in the stone opens into a hollow place from which a cool spring rises.

payload.title: Sennacherib's threat and Hezekiah's defence

aliases: king of Judah son of Ahaz
payload.name: Hezekiah
payload.note: Reforming king of Judah son of Ahaz who receives Isaiah.

stages.label: Hezekiah, king of Judah

quotes.quote: Hezekiah began to reign when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem.
And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
When King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into Yahweh’s house.

stages.text: Hezekiah: a man in his late twenties to forties, lean and upright, of Israelite stock. Olive-brown skin, close-trimmed dark beard, dark hair pinned under a royal fillet. Grave, weathered face. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of undyed linen under a deep-blue royal court robe with a woven gold border. Signature prop: a plain wooden royal staff.

payload.name: Sennacherib
payload.note: King of Assyria who besieges Jerusalem and is killed by his sons.

stages.label: Sennacherib, king of Assyria

quotes.quote: Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and took them.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, went home, and lived at Nineveh.

stages.text: Sennacherib: a man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and commanding; olive-brown skin; a full, carefully curled dark beard and short-cropped hair beneath a tall, conical royal crown banded with gold; a dark, strong face with heavy brows and a steady, severe gaze. He wears a long embroidered court robe of crimson and gold over a fringed tunic, with a deep-blue royal cloak, and bears a royal staff and an ornate gold-hilted sword at his belt.

payload.title: Peter on Jesus and David

payload.name: Simon Peter
payload.note: The fisherman apostle, first-called disciple and leader of the twelve, who appears in the Gospels, Acts, Galatians and both letters of Peter; all entries here are the same individual, distinguished only by role and portrayal.

stages.label: Simon Peter

quotes.quote: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas

stages.text: Simon Peter: a sturdy man in his thirties, broad-shouldered from hauling nets, weathered brown skin from sun on the Sea of Galilee, short dark curly hair and a full beard flecked with grey. Plain undyed tunic of natural linen under a rough brown wool cloak. Signature props: a coiled fishing net over one shoulder and a wooden fishing staff.

payload.title: The three visitors and Sarah's laughter

payload.name: The three visitors at Mamre and the two angels at Sodom
payload.note: The three men who visit Abraham and the two angels who rescue Lot in Genesis, treated as one group of visitors; not the two white-robed angels at the empty tomb in John.

stages.label: The visitors (typical member)

quotes.quote: The two angels came to Sodom at evening. Lot sat in the gate of Sodom.

stages.text: The visitors: men of mature adult age, neither young nor old; lean and sturdy build; skin weathered brown by desert sun; short dark beard and hair cropped close to the head; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen wrap over a short wool tunic in earth brown, with leather sandals. Carries a plain wooden staff, the only prop.

payload.name: Mamre (the oaks of Mamre)
payload.note: The oak grove near Hebron where Abraham dwells, receives the three visitors and buries Sarah; distinct from the town of Hebron itself, though the aliases overlap.

stages.label: The oaks of Mamre

quotes.quote: Abram moved his tent, and came and lived by the oaks of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and built an altar there to Yahweh.
the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field, the cave which was in it, and all the trees
Yahweh appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day.

stages.text: Mamre: a rolling upland grove near Hebron, in a dry hill country of limestone ridges and scrub. Great old terebinth and oak trees stand in a broad clearing, their wide trunks and grey-green canopies giving shade. Among them lie a level field with a cave at its edge, a spring or well nearby, and herders' tent-camps of dark goat-hair cloth. Low stone walls mark the field's bounds; no buildings beyond tents and altars of piled stone.

payload.title: Second tablets; God proclaims his name
Joseph's policy during the famine

payload.name: Joseph son of Jacob (the dreamer)
payload.note: Favorite son of Jacob and Rachel, sold into Egypt and later ruler under Pharaoh; the Genesis figure, also named in Judges as the house of Joseph's ancestor, Acts and Hebrews as the patriarch; not the husband of Mary.

stages.label: Joseph, son of Jacob

quotes.quote: Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brothers.
Joseph was well-built and handsome.
he made him a tunic of many colors.
arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.
Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt.
Joseph lived one hundred ten years.

stages.text: Joseph: a young man of about seventeen in youth, rising to a mature man of thirty and later an elder of one hundred ten; well-built and handsome, lean and strong from shepherding, with warm brown skin, dark hair cut short, a smooth-shaven face in Egyptian style, dark eyes and a steady, gentle expression. Signature outfit: a long tunic of many colours in Canaanite style, bright reds, blues and yellows; in Egypt, robes of white or cream fine linen. Signature props: a gold chain at the neck and Pharaoh's signet ring on the hand.

payload.name: Pharaoh of Joseph
payload.note: Egyptian king of Joseph's era who dreams of cattle and grain and elevates Joseph; the king who knew Joseph, distinct from the Exodus oppressor.

stages.label: Pharaoh of Joseph

quotes.quote: Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.

stages.text: Pharaoh of Joseph: man in his fifties; broad, dignified build; deep bronze skin; close-cropped dark hair under a tall blue and gold royal headcloth with a cobra emblem; neatly trimmed beard, ceremonial false beard; calm, grave face. Signature outfit: white pleated linen kilt and shendyt with a broad golden collar in blue and gold. Props: gold signet ring, gold chain, crook and flail of office.

payload.name: Egypt
payload.note: The land of Egypt where patriarchs sojourn, Israel is enslaved and plagues fall; recurs in Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Psalms, Ezekiel, Hosea, Micah and Hebrews as the same land.

stages.label: Egypt

quotes.quote: The land of Egypt is before you. Make your father and your brothers dwell in the best of the land.
Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen
But the midwives feared God, and didn’t do what the king of Egypt commanded them
for Memphis will become a desolation, and will be burned up, without inhabitant.

stages.text: Egypt: a long green valley of the Nile flanked by pale desert; broad river channels, canals and reed marsh; fertile black earth fields of barley and flax; date palms and sycamores; mud-brick and limestone cities with tall temple pylons, obelisks and fortified walls; the Delta with its towns of Goshen and Zoan.

payload.title: Praise and restoration of Zion

payload.name: Zion (holy hill / Mount Zion)
payload.note: The holy hill or temple mountain where Yahweh dwells and reigns, referred to as Zion, Mount Zion, or my holy mountain across psalms, joel, amos, micah, 1-peter and revelation; one hill identity, distinct from the city of Jerusalem.

stages.label: Zion, holy hill

quotes.quote: Beautiful in elevation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the north sides, the city of the great King.
As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so Yahweh surrounds his people from this time forward and forever more.
Walk about Zion, and go around her. Number its towers.

stages.text: Zion: a high rocky limestone hill rising above a ring of surrounding mountains, its slopes terraced with olive and fig trees and bordered by cedar-brown woods. Upon the summit stand the walled sanctuary courts of Yahweh's temple of pale stone and cedar, with tall gates and fortified towers along the walls of the city.

payload.title: Sisera and Jael; Barak defeats Jabin

payload.name: Deborah
payload.note: Prophetess and judge of Israel under her palm tree, wife of Lappidoth, who sends for Barak and sings the song of chapter 5; distinct from the other prophetesses in this group.

stages.label: Deborah, prophetess and judge

quotes.quote: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, judged Israel at that time.
She lived under Deborah’s palm tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim
Until I arose a mother in Israel.

stages.text: Deborah: woman of mature years, perhaps fifties, upright and steady; medium build; warm brown skin of the hill country; dark hair worn covered beneath a linen headcloth edged in blue; calm, dignified face with deep-set dark eyes and a firm mouth. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a deep ochre woven cloak with a blue border. Signature prop: a slender palm-wood staff of judgment carried alone.

payload.name: Barak
payload.note: Naphtali commander who fights Sisera at Mount Tabor.

stages.label: Barak

quotes.quote: She sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh Naphtali
Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali together to Kedesh.

stages.text: Barak: man in his prime, roughly thirty to forty years old; sturdy, broad-shouldered, weathered build from war and hill country; olive-brown skin; dark hair worn to the shoulder and a short, close-trimmed dark beard; steady, resolute face with a strong brow. Signature outfit: a woven undyed wool tunic with a long dark-red wool cloak fastened at the shoulder. Carries no props alone.

aliases: captain of the army of Hazor
payload.name: Sisera
payload.note: Captain of Jabin's army in Hazor who fought Barak and was killed by Jael; the 1 Samuel mention refers to the same Sisera, so both entries are one individual.

stages.label: Sisera, captain of Jabin's army

quotes.quote: the captain of whose army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth of the Gentiles.
Sisera gathered together all his chariots, even nine hundred chariots of iron

stages.text: Sisera: man in his forties, lean and hardened; olive-brown skin; dark hair cropped close with a short trimmed beard; a strong, weathered face with a grave, proud mouth. Signature outfit: a long woven tunic of deep blue-violet under a bronze-studded leather corselet, with a dark wool cloak in ochre. Carries alone a bronze-bladed sword at the hip.

payload.name: Jael
payload.note: Wife of Heber the Kenite who kills Sisera with a tent peg in her tent; the only Jael in these divisions.

stages.label: Jael

quotes.quote: the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite
Jael, Heber’s wife, took a tent peg, and took a hammer in her hand
Jael shall be blessed above women, the wife of Heber the Kenite

stages.text: Jael: a woman of about thirty-five to forty, sturdy and steady in build, with warm olive-brown skin weathered by desert sun. Dark hair is bound up and covered by a plain linen head cloth. Her face is calm, strong and grave. Her signature outfit, worn most often, is a long undyed woven wool tunic in deep indigo with a rust-red woven cloak. She carries a heavy iron tent peg and a hammer as her own tools.

payload.name: Heber the Kenite
payload.note: Kenite man, husband of Jael, whose tent Sisera flees to; not the Kenite people as a whole.

stages.label: Heber the Kenite

quotes.quote: Now Heber the Kenite had separated himself from the Kenites

stages.text: Heber the Kenite: a man in his middle years, sturdy and weathered, with a lean, sun-browned face and deep lines at the eyes. Skin dark bronze from desert sun. Short, dark hair and a close-trimmed beard streaked with grey. Steady, measured features. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven wool tunic of ochre-brown with a long dark-blue cloak fastened at one shoulder. Carries a tent peg and mallet as his sole props.

payload.name: Jabin king of Hazor
payload.note: King of Hazor leading the northern coalition at Merom.

stages.label: Jabin, king of Hazor

quotes.quote: When Jabin king of Hazor heard of it, he sent to Jobab king of Madon
Yahweh sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor

stages.text: Jabin, king of Hazor: a man of about fifty, broad-shouldered and upright; olive-brown skin; dark hair and a short trimmed beard streaked with grey; a lined, grave face with a strong nose and steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: a long fringed woollen robe in deep crimson over a white linen tunic, bound with a gold-threaded belt. Signature prop: a bronze-bladed sword in a worked leather scabbard at his hip.

payload.name: Hazor (capital of Jabin in Judges)
payload.note: Capital of King Jabin of Canaan in the period of the judges, the scene of Barak's defeat of Jabin and of Sisera's flight; a separate later city from the one burned in Joshua.

stages.label: Hazor, royal Canaanite capital

quotes.quote: Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor
there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite

stages.text: Hazor: a large fortified tell city on a rise above a fertile plain in northern Galilee, its high mud-brick and stone ramparts with a gate tower of dressed stone. Within the walls stand flat-roofed houses and a royal palace of cut stone and cedar beams, with a great water shaft cut down to springs. Olive groves, terraced vines and palms grow beyond the walls; chariot-ready roads run out across the plain. Earth tones: ochre, grey stone and pale limestone.

payload.name: Kedesh
payload.note: Town where Barak is summoned and where Heber's tent lies near the oak in Zaanannim.

stages.label: Kedesh

quotes.quote: out of Kedesh Naphtali
pitched his tent as far as the oak in Zaanannim, which is by Kedesh

stages.text: Kedesh: a fortified hill town of Naphtali in upland Galilee, built of rough-hewn limestone and mud brick with flat roofs and a low defensive wall. Terraced olive groves and vines climb the slopes; a great terebinth-oak stands near the edge of town beside the tents of the Kenites. Dry, golden grass and scrub cover the ridges.

payload.name: Mount Tabor
payload.note: Where Barak musters his men against Sisera in Judges.

stages.label: Mount Tabor

quotes.quote: Go and lead the way to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men
So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.

stages.text: Mount Tabor: a solitary, dome-shaped mountain rising abruptly from the broad plain of Jezreel in northern Israel; its slopes are rounded and grassed with terebinth and oak scattered among limestone outcrops; the summit is a flat, rocky crown; no buildings are visible on its open ridges, only low stone walls and ancient terraces; earth in ochre and olive tones.

payload.name: river Kishon
payload.note: Riverside battlefield where Sisera's chariots are swept away.

stages.label: River Kishon

quotes.quote: to the river Kishon, Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and his multitude
The river Kishon swept them away, that ancient river, the river Kishon.

stages.text: River Kishon: a broad, ancient, slow-moving river across the fertile plain of Jezreel, its banks lined with reeds, tamarisk and oleander, with low clay banks, muddy fords and soft silt that can swallow wheels. Low rounded hills rise in the distance, and the walled Canaanite towns of the plain stand on the heights beyond the water.

payload.name: Harosheth of the Gentiles
payload.note: Sisera's home city; his army retreats there.

stages.label: Harosheth of the Gentiles

quotes.quote: Sisera, who lived in Harosheth of the Gentiles.
from Harosheth of the Gentiles, to the river Kishon.

stages.text: Harosheth of the Gentiles: a fortified Canaanite town on a rise above the Kishon plain, with mudbrick and stone walls, a gate tower and flat-roofed houses of sun-dried brick. Olive groves and terraced fields of barley lie below, with the dry riverbed of the Kishon winding nearby.

payload.name: Deborah's palm tree
payload.note: Place in the hill country of Ephraim where Deborah judges Israel.

stages.label: Deborah's palm tree

quotes.quote: She lived under Deborah’s palm tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim

stages.text: Deborah's palm tree: a solitary tall date palm with a slender straight trunk and a crown of long fronds, rooted on a rocky terraced ridge in the hill country of Ephraim, between the villages of Ramah and Bethel. Stone walls and olive terraces run down the slopes; scrub oak and terebinth grow among limestone outcrops; a worn path leads up to the tree's shade.

payload.title: Mocking and Peter's denial

payload.name: Servant girl who questions Peter
payload.note: Unnamed maid in Matthew's account who accuses Peter of being with Jesus; distinct from Rhoda, the named servant girl at Mary's house in Acts, though both are servant girls who recognize Peter.

stages.label: Servant girl who questions Peter

quotes.quote: a maid came to him, saying, “You were also with Jesus, the Galilean!”

stages.text: Servant girl who questions Peter: late teens to early twenties; slender build; olive skin; dark hair bound back under a plain linen head covering; a modest, lined face with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a simple undyed linen tunic with a faded ochre wrap over the shoulders, in earth tones. Carries no props.

payload.name: The Roman soldiers
payload.note: Roman soldiers (and Herodian soldiers in Luke) who mock, crucify and guard Jesus across all three Gospels; they are one body of soldiers seen from different accounts, so all three entries describe the same group.

stages.label: The Roman soldiers

quotes.quote: Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the Praetorium, and gathered the whole garrison together against him.
The soldiers twisted thorns into a crown and put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple garment.
Now the tunic was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

stages.text: The Roman soldiers: adult men, late twenties to forties; sturdy, disciplined build; olive to tan skin of Mediterranean men; short-cropped dark or brown hair, clean-shaven or close-cropped beard; stern, weathered faces. Signature dress: a short tunic of undyed linen under a red-brown woollen military cloak, leather belt and sandals, bronze helmet worn at the cohort. Props: a short sword at the hip and a tall rectangular shield.

aliases: the court of the high priest
the courtyard of the high priest
payload.name: the court of the high priest (Caiaphas)
payload.note: Courtyard of Caiaphas where Jesus is tried and Peter denies him in Matthew; same court as the high priest's court in John, identified by Caiaphas and the trial setting.

stages.label: The court of the high priest

quotes.quote: the court of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas
He was sitting with the officers, and warming himself in the light of the fire.
entered in with Jesus into the court of the high priest

stages.text: The court of the high priest: an open paved courtyard of pale limestone flagstones inside a high-walled stone house in Jerusalem. A wide arched gateway with a timber door faces the street. A charcoal fire burns on a stone hearth at the centre of the court, and a stone porch with columns stands along one side. Olive and fig trees grow in clay pots by the walls; the upper walls are plastered and lit by torch sconces.
